verdict.rationale: MotherDuck documents natural-language analysis through its remote MCP server and Dives. Its Guides capture 'metric definitions, join conventions, and domain context' so agents produce accurate SQL, and governance comes from read-only MCP access and scoped Shares. However, the semantic grounding is markdown guidance supplied to an agent, not an enforced semantic layer that prevents hallucinated joins. missing for 10: an enforced or governed semantic model guaranteeing correct joins and metrics, a documented business-user NL experience beyond MCP and Dives prompts, independent or hands-on corroboration of answer accuracy.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, business users can ask questions in natural language and get governed, semantically-grounded answers rather than hallucinated joins

citations.quote: Read and write Guides — markdown documents that capture your org's metric definitions, join conventions, and domain context, so agents produce accurate SQL without repetitive prompting
The MotherDuck remote MCP Server lets you analyze your data using natural language and generate interactive visualizations, all without writing SQL.
To restrict your AI assistant to read-only access, see Restricting to read-only access
you can ask a question and save the answer as a Dive that stays current with your data.
